problem_statement: In the 6P neighbor simulation, the neighbor table is configured to hold at most 4 entries. After TSCH is started as coordinator, the test allocates three 6P neighbor entries sequentially. The third allocation is expected to be rejected (return NULL) because the table is full. Instead, the third allocation returns a valid pointer and the test fails. Required behavior: when the neighbor table has reached its configured maximum, a 6P neighbor allocation must return NULL.
causal_chain: The 6P neighbor test (test_alloc_and_free) starts TSCH as coordinator, which registers 2 virtual neighbor entries. The neighbor table is configured with a maximum of 4 entries. The test then allocates 3 6P neighbors and asserts that the third returns NULL. At base, the 3rd allocation returns a non-NULL pointer, causing the assertion to fail. After the production fix, the 3rd allocation returns NULL and the assertion passes. The other Cooja scenarios in the suite (sixtop, sixp-pkt, sixp-trans, sixp, sixtop-sf-error-handler) pass before and after.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: On a mote that participates in the TSCH MAC and also runs the 6top (6P) neighbor-management unit test, the 6P neighbor table behaves as if it has fewer usable entries than its configured capacity. The 6top neighbor allocations do not match the documented behavior: a node configured to hold exactly two neighbors ends up being unable to allocate, find and free 6P neighbor entries the way the test expects. The observable symptom is that the 6P neighbor unit test fails to complete successfully (its assertions about a neighbor being findable, allocatable, or rejected when the table is full do not hold) when the same node also operates the TSCH queue as a coordinator, instead of failing gracefully. The required behavior is that 6P neighbor allocation and lookup work correctly even though the TSCH queue holds its own entries in the same shared neighbor table, so the 6P neighbor unit test passes.
